recipes.name: Pumpkin Crumb Cake
ingredients_raw: 1 (15.25 ounce) package yellow cake mix, divided

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a 9x13-inch baking pan.
Reserve 1 cup of the cake mix in a medium bowl. Combine remaining cake mix, butter, and egg in a large bowl until well combined; press into the bottom of the prepared pan.
Mix pumpkin, white sugar, eggs, brown sugar, and cinnamon together in the large bowl until well combined. Pour over crust.
Stir sugar and butter into reserved cake mix until crumbly; sprinkle over pumpkin layer. Scatter walnuts over top.
Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean, 40 to 45 minutes. Cool completely in the pan on a wire rack before slicing.

raw_recipe.headline: Pumpkin Crumb Cake
raw_recipe.description: This pumpkin crumb cake has 3 delicious layers, starting with a buttery crust, topped with creamy pumpkin custard, and a crunchy nut topping.

review.reviewBody: This cake deserves more than 5 stars. This cake is the "BOMB". I added spices to my cake, like cinnamon, cloves, nutmeg, and allspice just because I alway's doctor up anything I make with pumpkin. I took it to a christmas party and it was a hit, everyone wanted the recipe by the end of the night. I brought the new French Vanilla cool whip to my friend's house who had the party and they all loved that too. They both went great toghether. OH and one last thing, I strongly recommend doubling the filling amount or the cake will be thin especially in a 9X13 pan.

My mother gave me a similar recipe 25 years ago and I have been making it for Thanksgiving every year since then.

Our filling recipe varies slightly in ingredients. Mine has 1 15 oz can pumpkin, 3/4 cup sugar, 1 tsp ground cinnamon, 1/2 tsp. salt, 1/2 tsp. ground ginger, 1/4 tsp. ground cloves, 2 eggs, 1 cup evaporated milk. This makes it more like true pumpkin pie in the middle.

Also, when putting the first layer in the pan, pat the bottom slightly higher on the sides to help keep the pumpkin filling in place.

I'm not sure I would make this again. It was ok, but it didn't knock y socks off as it seemed to for other reviewers. I made it in an oval Corningware baking dish approx. 8 x 11. My cake mix was 15.25 oz., so I added a couple of ounces of flour, 1/2 t. of baking soda and used jumbo eggs to make up the difference of the 18.25 oz. cake mix required. I did add some more spices to enhance the pumpkin part: cloves, ginger, allspice and nutmeg...along with the cinnamon it all equaled almost 2 t. We served it with a scoop of vanilla ice cream along side of the cake, and it's a good thing...it really needed it. I would suggest serving it with ice cream or whipped cream otherwise it's too dull and slightly dry. If I ever choose to make this again, I would double the filling part for sure...and add even more spice. I reduced the butter in the cake part by 2 T. and reduced the sugar in the topping by 1/4 c. due to many reviewers stating that it was too sweet. But I don't think these changes took away from the potential to be 5 star...it's just not a "wow" dessert overall. I really wanted to like it better than I did. Sorry Debbie. I will try other recipes instead.

I used pumpkin pie filling vs pumpkin puree for the pumpkin layer because it's what i had on hand. I mixed it with the eggs but simply omitted everything else. For the topping, instead of 1 cup of cake mix, I used 1/2 cup of cake mix and 1/2 cup of rolled oats. Everything else I followed exactly. It's delicious!

Since the cake mixes are much smaller now since this recipe was created, I only kept out about 3/4 cup of the dry mix that is saved for the topping, and just cut down on the sugar a bit in the topping. Otherwise, the crust is a bit thin. As written, I can only imagine this would be very bland on the spice. I added a 2 heaping TBSP of pumpkin pie spice, and also a bit of salt to the pumpkin filling. the salt helps to elevate everything; again otherwise is bland. great dessert, everyone raved.

Made this in the form of mini cupcakes to take to church for coffee hour. Per other reviewers suggestions, added 1/2 tsp each of cinnamon, nutmeg, allspice & ginger and 1/4 tsp cloves. Problem was the mini muffin tins were not deep enough to get enough pumpkin mixture in to get the flavor and crumb mixture would not stay on top of the cupcakes. Took ‘em to church anyway. Only two left at the end of the hour... and I ate those.
Made full size cupcakes out of the leftover mixtures and they were scrumptious.

Wonderful recipe....I did cut down the sugar in the toping to 1/4 cup and will add less to the pumpkin filling next time. I baked it in a glass decorative pie dish and it looked great when cut.....nice layers. Think a 9 x 13 pan would have made it look too thin. I also followed the suggestion to use ginger, nutmeg, allspice, cloves and cinnamon totaling the 1 1/2 tsp cinnamon that was called for in the recipe. Definitely will add this to our Thanksgiving menu for a nice change from regular pumpkin pie.

This was wonderful! I put 1 tsp cinnamon and 1/2 tsp allspice. I mixed the pecans into the crumble mix and it turned out wonderful. I also used an 8 x 11 pan and left in for an additional 10 mins. My 4 year old loved it even with the pecans!

Good Morning and Happy Holidays to All!

Made this early this morning to take to work.
Cooked in spring form pan for 1 hr.
Reduced sugar when noted to 1/3 cup instead of 1/2.
Added pecans to the cake base.
I sprinkled pecans on top of the crumble topping and they did burn a little so next time I will incorporate into crumble topping. 

Office thought this was a Winner!! Thanks for sharing.

I made this for a ladies function at church and was asked several times for the recipe. Needless to say there wasn't any leftovers. :) If I was to comment on the prep; the pan should be smaller for the ingredients listed, maybe 9x9. Add more pumpkin to the filling to make the finished product thick enough. It is too sweet as listed so I would decrease the amount of sugar next time. It comes out of the oven looking as good as it tastes. :)

I give this recipe a five-star because it turned out so delicious and I received praises from my in-laws even though it is the first time I ever made this cake. I did take the advice of previous reviewers and baked it in a 8x8 pan instead of a 9x13. You really would have to double the filling if you want it to fit in a 9x13 pan. And I sprinkled some nuts on the bottom of the crust before I add the filling, as well as on the top of the cake. Wonderful cake. This is definitely going into my favorite recipes collection.
simple but multiple steps - all necessary and it's delicious@

This is absolutely amazing in flavor and texture. My first try, I followed suggestions of doubling the pumpkin filling mix, which I definitely agree is a great idea. The problem I’m having as I’ve made it twice now, is the bottom cake layer seems to over bake (not burn) while allowing the double mix of pumpkin filling to finish baking. Maybe this is how it’s meant to be anyway? Maybe I’m expecting a softer cake like layer but instead it’s supposed to be more crust like? I don’t know how this can be resolved, but I’m sure someone out there will have a solution if it’s necessary.
Simple yet not the usual pumpkin dessert Definitely a crowd pleaser

I liked the idea of three layers, but I wanted more pumpkin custard than the recipe provided. I followed Mary F.'s featured tweak for a more of a pumpkin pie filling recipe, using evaporated milk, and doubled it. I added some flour and a little baking soda to the crust mixture so it would be thick enough, and I used a spice cake with pudding mix. I used cinnamon sugar and pecans for the topping. It came out great, and everyone loved it!
Would never make it again. Clumps of dry cake mix on the top. Too much cake and not enough pumpkin.
Too sweet! The topping does not need 1/2 cup sugar, there is sugar in the cake mix.
Omg!

Made this Tonite for Thanksgiving. It tastes great. I made in a pie tin because I need my 13x9 for cooking tomorrow. Probably over cooked it a little because I was worried it wasn't set up. The toothpick wouldn't come out clean. It just made the topping a little. More crumbly
Easy recipe for the Holidays.
